title: Microsoft Edge: watermarking protection for sensitive content
summary: Hold: the policy-precedence guidance omits Microsoft's documented exception that lets Edge management service policies override device policies. The preview behaviour and licensing are otherwise well sourced, but two assurances about data access and copying go beyond the documentation.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft identifies an audit action instead of a restriction as the most common cause of a missing watermark.
claims.quote: Verify the DLP/session/label policy carries a restriction (block) action, not just Audit. This is the most common cause.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: table
claims.claim: The Watermarking path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Microsoft Edge > configuration policy > Customization Settings > Security Settings > Watermarking.
claims.quote:
In the Edge Management Service (admin.microsoft.com → Settings → Microsoft Edge)
In your Configuration policy, navigate to Customization Settings → Security Settings.
Enable Watermarking for users who are receiving MAM policies.
claims.fix: Use 'Settings > Microsoft Edge > Configuration policies > configuration policy > Properties > Customization Settings > Security Settings > Watermarking'. The omitted tab lists the policies and Properties is the details page; the starting route is documented by the already cited https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-management-service.

claims.where: controls[0].api; front matter: changes; Governance controls
claims.claim: No Microsoft Graph operation or Edge policy for the Watermarking toggle is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge watermarking toggle Microsoft Graph API Edge policy reference watermark automation. Opened Edge Graph concept and API overview and learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-policies; searched the complete policy reference for watermark (no matches).

claims.where: Governance controls: policy precedence
claims.claim: Edge management service policies are overridden whenever they conflict with a GPO or MDM policy on the device.
claims.quote: If you want the Microsoft Edge management service policy to override MDM/GPM policy you can set the override in the EdgeManagementPolicyOverridesPlatformPolicy policy. This is a private policy and must be set via the registry.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'By default, conflicting device GPO or MDM policies override Edge management service policies; EdgeManagementPolicyOverridesPlatformPolicy can reverse that precedence.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-management-service.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The watermark adds no new data access.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge watermarking protection data access copying autonomous actions watermark display. Opened learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-management-watermark-protection and the DLP configuration page. They describe a browser overlay, not an assurance of no new data access.
claims.fix: Replace 'The watermark adds no new data access' with 'The browser renders a semi-transparent overlay across the content area' in Risk assessment and remove 'that adds no new data access' from the risk rationale. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-management-watermark-protection.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A watermark does not stop copying.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge watermarking protection data access copying autonomous actions watermark display. Read the feature and DLP configuration pages; they describe deterrence and separate restriction actions, but do not state that watermarking does not stop copying.
claims.fix: Replace 'A watermark does not stop copying' with 'Microsoft describes watermarking as a deterrent to unauthorised sharing'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-management-watermark-protection.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: No autonomous actions are described for the watermark.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge watermarking protection data access copying autonomous actions watermark display. Read the full feature page and DLP configuration page; they describe policy-triggered display and admin configuration, not autonomous actions.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls: table
claims.claim: The checklist tells readers to inventory DLP and Intune app protection policies and check Targeted Release, but those controls have no table rows.
claims.quote:
Inventory which Purview label, session and eDLP policies and which Intune app protection policies carry a block action.
Check ... that Targeted Release is enabled for the tenant.
Table: Whether Watermarking is turned on for a group of users.
claims.fix: Flag the Before rollout instructions to inventory Purview/Intune protection policies and check Targeted Release as checklist steps with no corresponding controls-table rows; do not add unverified paths or commands.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions
